workload: One 640x480 float32 depth-camera cloud (307200 xyz points) written as an ASCII PLY of double x, y, z.
notes: The writer keeps Tensor.tolist() of every float64 coordinate alive while it formats lines, so tracemalloc peaks at 49181792 bytes of Python objects for one VGA frame. Formatting the same shortest-round-trip text from the float64 buffer in chunks would drop that peak by well over 1 MiB and leave the file unchanged. Overlap: none of the 31 open kornia PRs touch PLY I/O; dexhunter's merged PRs #4581 #4583 #4584 #4587 #4588 are Denormalize, rgb_to_hls, plasma, RandomErasing and RandomCrop. Commits on this file since 2026-10-14 are docs only (#6487, #6393). The write loop last changed in September 2026 (#5048, #5033). header_size is already ignored; the function is not being moved.

workload: One 640x480 float32 depth-camera cloud (307200 xyz points) written as little-endian float64 binary PLY.
notes: The writer passes Tensor.tolist() into array.array('d'), so one call adds about 921650 live Python blocks, one float per coordinate. array.array.frombytes on the little-endian float64 buffer writes the same 24 bytes per point without those floats, far more than 5000 allocations. Overlap: no open PR and no dexhunter PR touch this function (dexhunter's five merged PRs are #4581 #4583 #4584 #4587 #4588). Since 2026-10-14 this file only received docs commits #6487 and #6393. The binary payload path is not deprecated.

workload: Read back the ASCII PLY of one 640x480 depth-camera cloud (307200 vertices, double x, y, z).
notes: The reader splits every vertex line and extends one Python list of floats before torch.tensor, peaking at about 921669 new blocks for 307200 points. A bulk parse into a preallocated buffer returns the same float32 (N, 3) tensor. Overlap: no open PR and no dexhunter PR (#4581 #4583 #4584 #4587 #4588) touch this reader. File commits since 2026-10-14 are docs only (#6487, #6393). The deprecated header_size argument is ignored; the parser itself is not being replaced.
